findings.title: Removing public `findMany` breaks service consumers
findings.body: The public `findMany(findManyArgs)` entry point is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment. No consumer is updated in this PR. Any caller that currently constructs `InsightsBookingService` and calls `findMany` (including passing `select`, `orderBy`, or extra `where` clauses) will fail to compile or throw at runtime. The conversion also removes the service's ability to execute/select data at all; callers must be migrated to call `$queryRaw` with `getBaseConditions()` or the old API must be preserved.

findings.title: Org-scope test is sensitive to unspecified repository ordering
findings.body: This assertion compares the exact order of IDs stored inside `Prisma.sql` values for `ANY(...)`. The service builds `teamIds` from `teamsFromOrg.map(...)` and `userIdsFromOrg` from `findAllByTeamIds(...)`, then de-duplicates with a `Set` without sorting. Unless those repository calls have an explicit ORDER BY (not shown or guaranteed), Postgres can return teams/members in a different order, so the test can fail nondeterministically even though `ANY` is order-insensitive. Sort IDs before building the SQL or compare normalized values.

findings.title: Caching tests were removed while caching logic remains
findings.body: The diff deletes the entire `Caching` describe block, but `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` are still part of the service. There is now no test that `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` reuse the cached SQL fragment on subsequent calls, so a regression that drops caching (extra membership/team queries per request) would go undetected.
